```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>")
library(linregpkg)
library(caret)
library(mlbench)
```

This vignette uses the BostonHousing data to compare ordinary linear
regression, forward selection, and ridge regression. The same training/test
split is used for each method. Ridge tuning is performed by 10-fold
cross-validation on the training set.

## Split the data

```{r data-split}
data("BostonHousing", package = "mlbench")
housing <- BostonHousing

set.seed(20261025)
train_rows <- caret::createDataPartition(
  housing$medv,
  p = 0.8,
  list = FALSE
)
training <- housing[train_rows, , drop = FALSE]
testing <- housing[-train_rows, , drop = FALSE]
predictor_names <- setdiff(names(housing), "medv")

c(training_rows = nrow(training), test_rows = nrow(testing))
```

The split is made before fitting any model. Model selection and tuning use
only the training rows; the test rows are held back for the final comparison.

## Linear regression and forward selection

The first model uses every predictor. The second starts with the intercept
and uses forward AIC selection with the full model as its upper scope. This
lets the search consider models containing zero through all predictors.

```{r fit-linear-models}
linear_fit <- stats::lm(medv ~ ., data = training)

upper_scope <- stats::reformulate(predictor_names, response = "medv")
forward_fit <- stats::step(
  stats::lm(medv ~ 1, data = training),
  direction = "forward",
  scope = list(
    lower = stats::as.formula("medv ~ 1"),
    upper = upper_scope
  ),
  trace = 0
)

length(attr(stats::terms(forward_fit), "term.labels"))
```

We report the training RMSE and R-squared for both models.

```{r training-metrics}
rmse <- function(actual, predicted) {
  sqrt(mean((actual - predicted)^2))
}

r_squared <- function(actual, predicted) {
  1 - sum((actual - predicted)^2) /
    sum((actual - mean(actual))^2)
}

training_performance <- data.frame(
  model = c("Linear regression", "Forward selection"),
  RMSE = c(
    rmse(training$medv, stats::predict(linear_fit, newdata = training)),
    rmse(training$medv, stats::predict(forward_fit, newdata = training))
  ),
  R_squared = c(
    r_squared(training$medv, stats::predict(linear_fit, newdata = training)),
    r_squared(training$medv, stats::predict(forward_fit, newdata = training))
  )
)
training_performance
```

## Tune ridge regression with caret

The custom caret model below delegates each fit to ridgereg. The package
centers and scales predictors, leaves the intercept unpenalized, and solves
the augmented least-squares problem using QR decomposition.

```{r caret-ridge-model}
ridge_model <- list(
  label = "QR Ridge Regression",
  library = "linregpkg",
  type = "Regression",
  parameters = data.frame(
    parameter = "lambda",
    class = "numeric",
    label = "lambda"
  ),
  grid = function(x, y, len = NULL, search = "grid") {
    if (is.null(len)) {
      len <- 15
    }
    if (search == "grid") {
      data.frame(lambda = 10^seq(-3, 3, length.out = len))
    } else {
      data.frame(lambda = 10^stats::runif(len, min = -3, max = 3))
    }
  },
  fit = function(x, y, wts, param, lev, last, classProbs, ...) {
    x <- as.data.frame(x, check.names = FALSE)
    response_name <- ".ridge_response"
    while (response_name %in% names(x)) {
      response_name <- paste0(response_name, "_")
    }
    x[[response_name]] <- as.numeric(y)
    formula <- stats::reformulate(".", response = response_name)
    linregpkg::ridgereg(formula, data = x, lambda = param$lambda)
  },
  predict = function(modelFit, newdata, preProc = NULL, submodels = NULL) {
    stats::predict(modelFit, newdata = as.data.frame(newdata))
  },
  prob = NULL,
  sort = function(x) x[order(x$lambda), ]
)

ridge_grid <- expand.grid(lambda = 10^seq(-3, 3, length.out = 19))
ridge_control <- caret::trainControl(method = "cv", number = 10)

set.seed(20261025)
ridge_fit <- caret::train(
  x = training[, predictor_names, drop = FALSE],
  y = training$medv,
  method = ridge_model,
  trControl = ridge_control,
  tuneGrid = ridge_grid,
  metric = "RMSE"
)

ridge_fit$bestTune
ridge_fit$results
```

The selected value of lambda is chosen by the lowest mean 10-fold
cross-validation RMSE. The final ridge model is then refit by caret on the
complete training set.

```{r ridge-training-performance}
ridge_training_prediction <- stats::predict(ridge_fit, newdata = training)
ridge_training_performance <- data.frame(
  model = "Ridge regression",
  RMSE = rmse(training$medv, ridge_training_prediction),
  R_squared = r_squared(training$medv, ridge_training_prediction)
)

rbind(training_performance, ridge_training_performance)
```

## Compare all models on the test set

```{r test-performance}
test_predictions <- list(
  "Linear regression" =
    stats::predict(linear_fit, newdata = testing),
  "Forward selection" =
    stats::predict(forward_fit, newdata = testing),
  "Ridge regression" =
    stats::predict(ridge_fit, newdata = testing)
)

test_performance <- data.frame(
  model = names(test_predictions),
  RMSE = vapply(test_predictions, function(prediction) {
    rmse(testing$medv, prediction)
  }, numeric(1)),
  R_squared = vapply(test_predictions, function(prediction) {
    r_squared(testing$medv, prediction)
  }, numeric(1)),
  row.names = NULL
)
test_performance
```

## Conclusion

The table reports the held-out test performance for all three models. The
following conclusion is generated from this split rather than assuming that a
particular model must always win:

```{r conclusion}
best_model <- test_performance$model[which.min(test_performance$RMSE)]
cat(
  "For this random split,",
  best_model,
  "has the smallest test RMSE:",
  round(min(test_performance$RMSE), 3),
  ". The selected ridge penalty was",
  ridge_fit$bestTune$lambda,
  "."
)
```
